This petition under Section 482 of CrPC filed by the petitioner- complainant challenging the order dated 14th of July, 2023 passed by the Court of Second Additional Sessions Judge, Ambedkar Nagar, District Indore in CRR No.76 of 2022 affirming the order dated 20th of September, 2022 passed by the Court of JMFC, Ambedkar Nagar, District Indore in UNCR Case No. 91 of 2022,
whereby the complaint filed by the petitioner has been rejected by the trial Court.

entities.text: Second Additional Sessions Judge, Ambedkar Nagar, District Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
It is the case of the petitioner complainant that a land was allotted in the name of his father Late Ambaram i.e. 4800 sq.ft. in 1962 by Griha Nirman Sahakari Sanstha Maryadit, Ram Nagar,
Bhaislay, Tehsil Mhow, District Indore on 10th of January, 1979 after paying the sale consideration.
His father had four sons out of which, Rameshwar died and the share of Late Rameshwar was purchased by him and his brothers Murari and Mahesh on 26th of April 1994.
He, his deceased brother Murari and accused respondent NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35508 2 MCRC-40021-2023 No.1 Mahesh have 1/3-1/3 share in the said land.
It is further alleged that the said land has not been properly divided between him, his two brothers and their heirs.
As per the family partition, he has 20''x80'' share near the south wall of his private house and respondent No.1 has a 20''x80'' share after that, towards the south.
Rrespondent no.1 in collusion with other co-accused /respondents Nos.2 to 4 illegally sold the said plot to accused respondent No.5.
Wife of deceased Murari and son Rahul sold 30''X80'' ft. of land instead of 20''X80'' ft. on 24-09-2015.
Respondent No.1 also sold 10''x80'' ft. of his 1/3rd share to respondent No.5.
It was further alleged that all the respondents- accused want to usurp his share by conspiring and they have executed a forged sale deed.
Despite that, they are trying to build a house on the said plot in question.

sentences.text: The respondents- accused conspired and sold his ancestral plot of 20''x80'' ft. owned by him on the basis of fake and forged sale deed.
Therefore, a request was made by him to take cognizanceagainst the respondents accused for offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of IPC.
On the basis of which, statements of complainant and other witnesses were recorded.
After this, the complaint filed by him was dismissed by the trial Court vide order dated 20th of September, 2022.
Being aggrieved, a revision was filed by him before the revisional Court and same has also been dismissed by impugned order.
Being dissatisfied, the instant petition has been filed by him.

It is contended on behalf of petitioners that the learned trial Court has committed a serious error of law and fact by not closely examining the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35508 3 MCRC-40021-2023 documents available on record and passed the impugned order which is contrary to law.
The learned trial Court has also committed a serious error law by not examining statement of respondent No.5 and affidavit of Secretary of Gram Panchayat concerned.
Further, the learned Trial Court has also committed an error of law in not considering complainant's statements and documents produced therein.
The revisional Court has also committed an error in affirming the order passed by the Trial Court, without re-appreciating evidence and documents.
Hence, prayed for setting aside the impugned orders.
Heard learned Counsel for the petitioners at length.
Perused the impugned orders and documents available on record.
On perusal of the impugned orders, it is apparent that petitioner complainant has failed to produce any documentary evidence in regard to prove his ownership.

Contention of petitioner- complainant that respondents- accused usurped his share of land by conspiring and by means of execution of forged deed is concerned, the same will be proved by hand writing expert report but no substantial evidence has been proved on behalf of petitioner to prove the alleged forged and fabricated sale deed.

Certified copy of Civil Suit No.216-A of 2022 in which the application filed under Order 39 Rule 1 and 2 of CPC clearly reflects that a civil suit has been going on between the rival parties but the copy of the said order does not show as to whether civil suit has been decided finally or not.
From the statements of petitioner- complainant as well as documents produced on his behalf, it appears that matter appears to be of civil in nature.
He has utterly failed to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:35508 4 MCRC-40021-2023 produce any documentary evidence in respect of his title.
Even, if it is accepted that the disputed plot in question was sold by respondents, then petitioner- complainant has a civil right to get sale deed declared void before the Civil Court concerned.
This Court does not find any illegality or perversity in the impugned orders passed by two Courts below.
The impugned order passed by the revisional Court confirming the order passed by the trial Court is hereby affirmed.

In view of above discussion, this Court is of the considered opinion that since dispute is of civil in nature, no case is made out warranting interference by exercising inherent powers under Section 482 of CrPC by this Court.
The petition being devoid of merits, is hereby dismissed.
(HIRDESH) JUDGE MKB Suresh Choudhary vs Mahesh on 12 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/148557766/
